summary: The Detroit Lions beat the Las Vegas Raiders 26-14 on Monday Night Football at Ford Field on Oct. 30, 2023, bouncing back from a blowout loss in Baltimore. Rookie Jahmyr Gibbs led the way with 189 scrimmage yards and a touchdown, while the Lions defense sacked Jimmy Garoppolo six times. Detroit out-gained Las Vegas by 329 yards but left points on the board, including a Jared Goff pick-six, before moving to 6-2 and into their bye.
one_line: The Lions beat the Raiders 26-14 on Monday Night Football behind rookie Jahmyr Gibbs's 189 scrimmage yards and a dominant defense.
key_facts: The Detroit Lions beat the Las Vegas Raiders 26-14 on Monday, Oct. 30, 2023, at Ford Field in Detroit; kickoff was 8:15 p.m. ET.
The Lions out-gained the Raiders by 329 yards but missed chances in the red zone and had two turnovers deep in Raiders territory.
Jared Goff threw a 74-yard pick-six to Marcus Peters in the third quarter, cutting the Lions' lead to 16-14.
Rookie Jahmyr Gibbs had 189 scrimmage yards and a touchdown, including a 27-yard TD run, and recorded the first 100-yard rushing game of his career with David Montgomery out.
Amon-Ra St. Brown notched his third consecutive 100-yard game despite being listed as questionable with an illness.
Jimmy Garoppolo completed just 10 passes and was sacked six times; he repeatedly missed a wide-open Davante Adams, who finished with 11 yards.
Josh Jacobs led the Raiders' only first-half touchdown drive, scoring the game's first touchdown in the second quarter.
Lions rookie Sam LaPorta caught his fourth touchdown of the season to make it 16-7 before halftime.
Riley Patterson made his first four field goals, including from 44 and 52 yards, then missed a 26-yard attempt late.
The Lions improved to 6-2 and entered their bye in sole possession of the No. 2 seed in the NFC.
The Raiders lost their second straight game to an NFC North opponent and face a potentially must-win game against the Giants in Week 9.
Detroit had won four of its last five matchups with the Raiders; Las Vegas won the last meeting in 2019.
Jack Harlow was announced as the performer for the Lions' Thanksgiving Halftime Show.
Joe Buck and Troy Aikman called the game, with Lisa Salters reporting from the sideline.
